You will meet and question many NPCs throughout the game - talk to them carefully and wisely to gleam key information.

158398.overview:
Sequel to Jeff Minter's REVENGE OF THE MUTANT CAMELS. 
REVENGE II was published 4 years before its predecessor on the Amiga, which finally saw a shareware release in 1992.

158399.overview:
Rings of Medusa is a strategy game with light role-playing and business simulation elements. Located in a medieval kingdom, the game puts the player in control of the former king's son. Unfortunately, an evil sorceress called Medusa has taken control of the country and is now dominating the people.

The prince's task is to find five magical rings that will give him the power to overthrow the sorceress and claim back his heritage. In the beginning the hero will try to earn money by doing trade between different towns, or try his luck at bounty hunting or at treasure hunts. Once enough money has been earned to maintain a larger army, the prince will send forth his men to search for the rings which are in the possession of large soldier of fortune armies rallying the lands.

Sometimes the player takes part in small arcade sequences like sword fighting and sea fights, or controls an army on the battle field.

158400.overview:
A creative turn-based strategy game. Form a team of robots serving different roles and program them to eliminate the enemy from the arena. 

You have 5 different types of robots at your disposal, each with it's own weaponry and capabilities. The competition is run in a number of intervals giving you time to reprogram your robots and set them loose to destroy your opponent. 

This game includes multiplayer options for both multi-computer setups and hot seat play. There is no luck and reflexes are not a factor. Only the one with the best strategy will prevail.

158401.overview: Collect the required amount of diamonds and find the exit. This without running out of fuel and crash into the walls. There are 50 levels and graphics change every 5th level. Michael Klinge designed the game maps and Mathias Reichert wrote the copy-protection.

158402.overview:
Robot Readers ' story of Chicken Little helps children learn to read, is fun, and is easy-to-use. Electronically generated voice reads aloud with each word changing color as itis read. Speed of reading is easily adjusted. Children can point to a word in the text and hear it slowly sounded out by syllables and letter sounds. When animals in the picture are selected, their names are spoken and their colors change. Children can "turn the pages" by pressing either mouse button on the page icon. "Find the Word Game" asks the child to locate a word in the text with the pointer. When the correct word is found, the word will change color, and the child will hear a rewarding "beep". 

This game provides an exciting way to learn to read. Chicken Little will hold a young child's attention while developing early reading skills.

158403.overview:
The 3 classic fables of The Tortoise and the Hare, The City Mouse and The Country Mouse, and Belling the Cat are presented in this charming early reading program. Beautiful illustrations combine with built-in-word games to hold even a very young child's attention. Early reading skills are
enhanced as each story is read and words are highlighted. This interactive program allows children to "point" to objects in the illustrations, hear them identified, and see them "glow" on the screen. "Find the Word" game asks the child to locate a word in the text. When the word is
correctly identified it is highlighted and a rewarding "beep" is heard. 
This program's facility to foster early reading skills is combined with a positive computing experience. These classic tales with familiar and meaningful themes make Aesop's Fables a worthwhile addition to a young child's program collection.

158404.overview: The countdown rolls... The ultimate wheelchair challenge, a game like this contains 6 portions of sadism, 4 portions of joystick-destruction and immense fun!!! Playing it will surely lead into addiction. Released August 1,1992 at the Prime 92 party in Holland.

158406.overview:
Nearly 5 years before Rebel Assault and other fully-rendered CD-ROM titles popularised the rail-shooter gameplay, Tynesoft used it for a game with an unusual setting. You are on board a roller coaster which has been layered with targets to shoot out. 

The roller coaster follows its natural path, swinging from side to side and up and down, while you aim a turret at the targets and shoot them out. After completing its cycle, the roller coaster reverses, moving through the same area moving backwards. A co-operative two player mode exists, in which each player controls a crosshair. Make sure to hang on as the ride turns.

158407.overview: Released in 1990 on Amiga Fun issue 11 and 1992 on Amiga Fun Gold Edition issue 2. A funny and at the same time gripping game of skill. Cross dangerous roads without getting run over. Great graphics and realistic traffic noise put you right in the middle of the game. With digitized sound effects!

177873.overview: Adaptation of the board game from FASA, the game offers a space fighter phased combat, in both skirmish and a campaign mode. The player may play as either side, the Terran Overlord Government or the Commonwealth Rebels.

177874.overview: The Return of Medusa, also known as The Return of Medusa: Rings of Medusa II, is a 1991 role-playing video game and strategy video game hybrid developed by X-Ample and published by Starbyte Software for Amiga, Atari ST and PC DOS as a sequel to the 1989 game Rings of Medusa. A planned Commodore 64 version was cancelled.

177988.overview: The trolls are posing a threat to humanity, and it's your job to sort them out in this traditional-style platform game, which features over 200 screens. You have a gun and bolts of energy available to protect you. The graphics have detailed sprites but very plain backdrops, in an attempt to create a mood. Unusually a construction kit is included, allowing you to design your own levels down to the last detail. Another novelty is the option of mouse control on 16-bit systems, a seemingly impractical option for a platform game.

178221.overview:
This football simulation focuses on international football, allowing you to play a tournament or single friendly matches. Up to 8 human players can be involved in the tournament. Options include three skill levels, variable match lengths and a choice of sound or music (or both on some versions).

The match is viewed from the side, although it switches to a 3D view when the ball is close to the goal. The ball roughly sticks to the player's foot. Set pieces are controlled by moving an aiming cross-hair.

178223.overview:
This is a remake of Rings of Medusa. Basically identical to the original in gameplay, the remake offers enhanced graphics, hardware supported sound and an improved interface. 
 
Rings of Medusa is a strategy game with light role-playing and business simulation elements. Located in a medieval kingdom, the game puts the player in control of the former king's son. Unfortunately, an evil sorceress called Medusa has taken control of the country and is now dominating the people.

The prince's task is to find five magical rings that will give him the power to overthrow the sorceress and claim back his heritage. In the beginning the hero will try to earn money by doing trade between different towns, or try his luck at bounty hunting or at treasure hunts. Once enough money has been earned to maintain a larger army, the prince will send forth his men to search for the rings which are in the possession of large soldier of fortune armies rallying the lands.

Sometimes the player takes part in small arcade sequences like sword fighting and sea fights, or controls an army on the battle field.

178224.overview: Rolling Thunder is the world's most powerful secret police force and you are its best agent. Your mission is to stop an underground conspiracy to conquer the world and to save agent Leila, who has been captured. Starting out armed only with a handgun, you have to make your way through heavily guarded hallways and secret passages to find Leila and stop the enemy.

178225.overview: Although the title may cause it to appear pornographic, Romantic Encounters at the Dome is actually more of a text-based adventure that journeys deep into human behavior studies. It takes place at an important social event, where you try to pick up members of the opposite sex and either get your desires quenched, or be rejected, depending on what they think of you by your social interactions. The game may feature explicit textual descriptions of sexual intercourse.

178226.overview:
This game recreates the battle in 1879 where a British outpost at Rorke's Drift manned by 137 men managed to repel an attack by force of over 4,000 Zulu warriors.

This is a real-time strategy game where the player can pause the game and issue orders during a command mode, after which the orders are carried out and the battle progresses. You can only play as the British and two scenarios are available - one where the Zulus will attack according to the historical Order of Battle and deployment, and the other where the Zulus vary their strategy of attack.

Individual troops are represented in the game as animated soldier miniatures, with the player being able to move individual soldiers, resolve individual hand-to-hand combat situations and order a variety of different firing positions for each soldier.

180314.overview:
Raid Over Moscow is a Commodore 64 classic brought roaring back to life on the Commodore Amiga!

In this cold war thriller, a team of space-based commandos must save the U.S. from a Soviet nuclear strike! 

Requirements (for an actual Amiga): 



-  68000 and up
- OCS, ECS or AGA
- 1MB of Chipram OR 512KB Chipram, 512KB Slow Ram
- Floppy disk drive, OR
- 1MB of Hard Drive Space, OR
- CD-ROM - including CDTV and CD32



Full Game Description:

The USSR has launched a huge attack on the USA, and the only hope for the free world is for you (as leader of a US Squadron of fighters) to destroy their defense bases. This is done in a multi-stage action game with some similarities to the same developer's Beach Head. All the mini-games must be completed before the time limit on the bomb is expired.

The first thing you will see is a missile being launched; the game then takes you to your hangar, from which you must quickly launch as many ships as possible, a task made difficult by the limited gravity. You must then fly it into Soviet airspace in a side-view shoot 'em up section, in which staying low keeps you safe from radars, and quick reactions see you shoot enemy fighters and avoid trees.

The next scene takes place on a single-screen view, with five windows to shoot through, and enemies aiming at you to be avoided. You then reach the base, and must shoot out approaching enemies. Finally, you must use discs onto a wall, such that they rebound to hit maintenance robots, with the ultimate goal of causing the base to overheat, the Soviet attack to be thwarted, and the US to be saved.

181440.overview: "RasterBike" is a computer adaption of the motorbike race inspired by the movie "Tron". Two racers ride their futuristic motorbikes on the squared arena. The motorbikes leave the solid light trail which is fatal for any motorbike that will collide with it. The aim of the game is to conquer the opponent by making him to crash in the wall what makes him to lose one of nine lives. The game can be played with a computer or human opponent.

181441.overview: A game very much like Scrabble for up to four players, created by WSOY Micro and released by WSOY Productions in 1988.

181442.overview: Identify the picture that is different, find the odd man out. Number of sequences varies from 4 to 16 on two levels of difficulty. Supports 5 languages.

181443.overview:
Rectangle is fundamentally a variation of Konami’s Quarth with some Arkanoid style elements.

The basic lay takes’ place on a single screen - the player controls a small character on the bottom of the display which can be moved to the extreme left and right of the play-field. Tetris-like block shapes descend from the top of the screen. The player can shoot projectiles which become square units upon contacting the blocks.

The aim of the play is to form rectangles or squares by way of filling in the remaining space on the vertical, or horizontal level of the blocks to score points, and when all are cleared, the next level is unlocked. Some blocks contain an ever-cycling power up - which if converted, will cause a bonus collectable to fall, e.g. giving the ability to eliminate blocks with one shot, faster player movement & shots, or even transform the players’ sprite into a bat & ball for Breakout inspired play.

The game is divided into phases - called worlds, which consists of three levels, of which each world has a unique visual theme. A six-digit code is given at the successful conclusion of each world in order to keep progress.

181444.overview: Renegade III was the third and last in the Imagine's series, based on the original coin-op by Taito. The hero's girlfriend has been beamed into the future, while the man himself has been sent back into prehistory. This sets the scene for a sideways scrolling arena combat game, where the player fights in various time periods. The settings varied from Egyptian and medieval, to a futuristic level. As such, gone are the attacks of street gangs from the first two iterations of the series, replaced by assailants such as knights in armor and robots. In each level you have six minutes to reach the finish, as this is all the time the time-travel portal is available for. There are many surface hazards to avoid, as well as multi-layered Green Beret-style areas. You can kick and punch at different heights, allowing you to deal with each of the diverse foes.

181447.overview: Risk: A Gambling Game of Skill & Chance is a gambling game, developed and published by Joker, which was released in Australia in 1987

181459.overview:
Just as the German version of this gameshow was based on the US Jeopardy game show, this 1993 video game appears to be based on the 1987 Jeopardy video game but with enough changes aside from the language to make it stand on its own. 

Three players compete against each other by coming up with the question for a given answer. There are two rounds of play each with six categories of answers, and one final round consisting of a single answer. Each correct question given can be worth from $100 to $1000 for the player to respond first, or if a daily double is uncovered the player to find it may bet up to the current amount of money they have. The player with the most money at the end wins. Jeopardy! features a high scores table so players can save their characters wins and losses, different male and female character animations to choose from, and of course a wide variety of answers and questions. Up to three human players can compete, or a combination of human and computer players.

181463.overview: Ritter is a strategy game, developed and published by Ariolasoft, which was released in Europe in 1989.

181464.overview:
Although then a successful cricket player, Robin Smith licensed a management game. Playing against the computer, you can play a single match or a series of 3 or 5 one-day matches, as one of the top 7 international sides. These matches can be anywhere between 40 and 60 overs per side in length.

First you select your team off 11 based on their battling, bowling and wicket-keeping abilities. A coin toss decides who bats first, after which you choose your tactics for the upcoming over, based on weather and wicket conditions. The bowling side has 9 field layouts to choose from.

The action is represented from a top-down view of the whole field, with a running commentary as to the results of each stroke, showing what type of shot was played, who fielded the ball, and how many runs were scored.

181471.overview:
ROX is a hidden game within the Lotus Esprit Turbo Challenge game. It is activated by entering player one’s name as “MONSTER” and player two’s name as “SEVENTEEN”. The hidden game only works on versions of LOTUS 1 where the game information screen is shown after pressing fire to start it.

It was also published as a standalone game on the Coverdisk #4 of Amiga Action Magazine issue 18 (Mar 1991).

181472.overview: Rugby League Coach is a rugby management simulation, developed by  Anglosoft Visual Systems, and published by Audiogenic Software., which was released in Europe in 1994.

181476.overview:
Robot Commander is a real-time strategy game without a background scenario which goes beyond "science-fiction with robots". It is designed to be played with two players, but fighting against the AI is also an option.

Each player commands an army of robots with the goal to defeat the other player, mainly the opponent's headquarter. The game screen is quartered: a half goes to each player and this half is also split in half by itself. The upper part shows the map around the active robot (everything beyond its line of sight is blacked out) while the under part is dedicated to the menus in which the player chooses the robots and gives them commands. Examples of possible actions are patrolling, attacking, transporting droids (smaller robots) on a big robot or the "follow" command which can be used for moving larger squads. Another option is to repair destroyed, hostile robots and use them for the own army. Since the player can only control one robot at a time, they automatically follow the orders in absence until there is a reason to stop.

A special feature is that players not only compile their army out of 20 pre-defined robots before the match starts, but they also have the option to use an editor to create new ones or alter the statistics of existing robots. Options for the map are pre-defined, randomly generated or built with an editor. Likewise the starting positions can be picked or randomly chosen.

181477.overview:
The Computerized Coloring Books is a collection of three games developed by Capstone Software and published by its parent company IntraCorp for both the DOS and Amiga systems. 

The games are based on Bill Kroyer's film FernGully: The Last Rainforest, Don Bluth's film Rock-a-Doodle, and John Hughes's film Home Alone. The Rock-a-Doodle game was as released with Trolls and An American Tail: The Computer Adventures of Fievel and His Friends on the Capstone CD Game Kids Collection.

The games work as basic computerized coloring books, which require the player to fill in a lineart picture. There are 16 colors available, although they can be mixed to get up to 256 colors. The player can choose from a selection of backgrounds and add any characters to the picture, both of which are based on scenes and characters of the respective films. The products support a wide range of printers for the time of its release, including dot matrix, colour and laser printers.

181478.overview:
A rather simplistic Boulder Dash clone, you play a pink-haired miner who has to collect all the diamonds on a fixed-screen level. You must avoid falling boulders, which squish you, or getting trapped, which results in you having to commit suicide, losing a life and starting the screen again. You have five lives and must complete all 20 levels. Each level is timed.

The puzzles involve you excavating sandy-coloured rock to reach pink, man-sized diamonds. If you excavate a section of sand beneath a boulder, the boulder falls, killing you if you remain beneath it. You can push boulders, providing there is empty space on the other side (a la Sokoban), but you cannot pull them.

The game scores you 10 points per collected diamond, but there are no high scores available, nor is there anything after you complete the game. In fact, if you complete level 20 without creating a new level in the editor, the game will simply hang, forcing you to restart your Amiga. If you create new levels, you are only able to play them after you've completed the first 20 levels. Again, if you complete the last level you created (e.g. level 21), the game will simply crash as it tries to load the next level (e.g. level 22) and cannot find it.

181479.overview: Rugby Coach is a Rugby sports game, developed by Masters Of Strategy and published by CDS, which was released in Europe in 1992. Rugby Coak is a 1-4 player rugby management simulation which features include: Rugby League 1st and 2nd division; Rugby Union 3 Divisions, 3 Cups, full yearly calendar. Full player names and editors and the international scene. Five Nations, Grand Slam Triple crown and much more.

181676.overview: Regent is a strategy game, developed by Martin Economic Simulations and published by Linel, which was released in Europe in 1992

192726.overview: A single-player horizontally scrolling shooter created by Gabriel Leroy and team at Computer Adventure Dream. It was to be published by Ubi Soft, but never was released.

195567.overview:
Rollerpede is a single player Centipede type game.

In this game the player controls a gun which can be moved left/right the bottom of the playfield. A centipede starts at the top odf the screen and gradually works its way down the screen, the player's task is to destroy it but when it is shot the body breaks into two sections each of which moves independently.

200794.overview: RESHOOT R is a super reactive game for classic Amiga hardware, a horizontal scrolling shoot-'em-up with lots of enemy objects and how to avoid them. The game features adrenaline gameplay, high-quality animation, a balanced difficulty curve, wicked graphics such as organic fog effects, jerk-free parallax scrolling, and finally the experience of many objects, some small, some big like you've never seen on the Amiga before.

200795.overview: Rick Dangerous 2.5 is a one level demo of Rick Dangerous II not available in the full Rick Dangerous II game.

200815.overview:
Having just completed his great port of Bombjack (aka Bombjack: Beer Edition) in 2018, Graeme Gowie shifted his sights to one of Tecmo’s 1986 arcade releases – Rygar, a game never previously released on the Amiga platform.

Rygar is a side-scrolling platform game that sees you take control of a dead warrior who has risen from his grave to rid the land of Argool from the evil King Ligar. To achieve his objective, Rygar will have to navigate through various landscapes battling 22 different types of enemies using his long chain with a shield attached to the end of it.  Along the way, you will collect various power-ups that enhance your attacking capabilities and ramping up your points score to obtain valuable extra lives.

201313.overview: R.A.Y. Pokeri is a video poker card game based on common Finnish video poker machine. Keyboard is used to control game. No mouse or joystick needed.

205600.overview: Released 1992-04-03 on Amigo! issue 02/92. An editor is included on the disk. A single screen shooter, like Galaga with the added fun of dropped upgrades and items that alter gameplay and boss levels.

207376.overview:
Created by Harald Müller (Mueller) and published by Intersoft. An endless runner type game as we see many of these days. Guide the ball along the obstacle track that sprawls out into the horizon in space. Different colors will have different impacts on your ball.

The game is a clone of the classic game Trailblazer, which was first developed by Shaun Southern (one of the founders of Magnetic Fields, who developed the Lotus series)  for the Commodore 16/Plus 4 computers.

208650.overview: Green Beret​ ​is a run and gun game developed and released by Konami in arcades in 1985. It was ported to home systems, becoming a critical and commercial success for arcades and home computers. It was released as Green Beret internationally, and as Rush'n Attack in North America as a play on "Russian attack"​ ​ due to its Cold War setting. It is remembered for​ this Cold War setting and its reliance on the player using mainly a knife to dispatch enemies, although you were able to collect many different weapons including the flame thrower. ​Developer Dante Mendes has finally released the Arcade conversion of Green Beret which has been developed for the Amiga using Earok's Scorpion Engine.

211236.overview: A puzzle game based on Sokoban levels. It has great music, smooth scrolling, supports passwords for each level and has a level editor. published in Amiga Fun (UK) no. 6, Apr 1991, Amiga Mania no. 3, Jun 1992  and in Amiga Fun Gold Edition (DE) no. 2, 1993. A collision of the space vessel Vega VII with an asteroid rips tertium containers filled with plasma away from its anchors. The plasma containers must be fastened down again with the help of  a droid, which you control! All containers must be pushed to an anchor. A control lamp on top of the container indicates when it is secure. The level finishes when all the containers are correctly secure. Do it in as few moves as possible.

211428.overview:
Conversion from the original ST version:

The universe is under attack (again). On EMAR II, home of some rare energy crystals, an alien fleet stopped by. Defence is reduced to a single turret gun named "Kiss My Ass".

Recoil is a Defender clone. You control the ship and can scroll to both left and right by turning your ship into the desired direction. A huge radar map on the bottom of the screen show enemy activities. In the game, there is a twist on the original scheme: your ship is mounted on some building on the top of the screen and therefore constantly rising back to the top of the screen, which makes control a bit more challenging.

The goal is to destroy any moving enemy, while collecting energy and bringing those energy crystals to your base. You have three lives initially and can release a smart bomb as emergency exit.

211431.overview:
Psytronik Software is proud to present ROTATOR, a previously unreleased arcade game for the Commodore Amiga. Take control of your ROTATOR craft and carefully manoeuvre it through the varied challenging landscapes collecting diamonds whilst trying to stay above the ever-rising flood level!

This game contains an amazing replay feature where is basically records everything you do in real-time. If you fail at a level you can replay the recording of your progress and then resume control of the game at any time. 
 
Rotator was was initially developed in the mid 90s by Tim Gilbert and Shaun Watters as a Licenceware game. The success of Black Dawn Rebirth prompted an updated version of Rotator with new music, graphics and levels. Initially intended to be released as "Rotator 2", the number was dropped due to the obscurity of the original.

211471.overview: Amiga Game: RetroWars Episode IV 1/4 (2018): The release of multi-language versions:, French, German and English, along the Spanish version 1.4 the release of the boxed commercial version, leads us to bring here and now this great and fun AmigaWave game. A graphic adventure in a very distant galaxy but with funny dialogues, well done caricatures and very well finished. Turn yourself into Luk, followed by your droids and his master, in order to escape from the planet and the negative influence of retro-speculation, promoted by the dark side.

211543.overview: Overhead/Top down racing for one or two players created by Philip G. Harle and released in 1993.

211571.overview:
Relics of Deldroneye is the first in a series of 3 point & click graphic adventure games. In this sci-fi/fantasy story, you play the role of Royal Venturex Falcon. As the game begins, Falcon is languishing in a filthy cell, imprisoned for theft. He must find a way to escape the prison, and get to the planet Zantis.

The interface splits the screen vertically: the top half of the screen shows the current scene, and underneath is a panel that shows the items that Falcon is carrying, as well as ten action buttons ("Move", "Look", "Take", "Use", "Talk", "Open", "Close", "Give", "Offer" and "Show"). The action panel also has secondary tabs that give contextual information about important characters, and displays the length of time that you have been playing.

211572.overview: A point and click adventure that is a sequel to Relics Of Deldroneye: Book One - Falcon And The Medivians and Precursor to Relics of Deldroneye 2: Island of Debreen.

211573.overview:
Island of Debreen is a sci-fi/fantasy point & click adventure game, part of the Relics of Deldroneye saga. The main character Falcon, once-loyal to Deldronis royalty but now living alone in exile, has at least acquired his own full-size spacecraft to get around in. As the game begins, Falcon's ship is dangerously low on power and drifting through space, after barely escaping from an altercation with an unidentified hostile vessel. Falcon must carefully conserve remaining power between the ship's various sub-systems, and work out what to do next...

The interface splits the screen vertically: the current scene is shown in third-person perspective, above a panel which displays Falcon's current inventory items, and also a number of action buttons: "Move", "Look", "Take", "Use", "Talk", "Help", "Open", "Close", "Give" and "Show".

211682.overview:
Simple and well made puzzle game. Shouldn’t take that long to finish. In Redpill Puzzle you move around a blue jewel and try to push the green and
purple jewels to the exit. However there is a red jewel that stands in the way so get rid of it however you can. This puzzle game is inspired by games like Sokoban and Atmomic.

211685.overview: A little fanmade Rick Dangerous remake made in the gameeditor Backbone by the EAB member mjnurney. You play Rick Dangerous, an Indiana Jones type who's on a quest. Rick Dangerous is a platform game across many screens, in which Rick has his gun in one hand, and dynamite sticks in another. You must take a methodical approach to clearing each screen, as there are traps in place which will need memorizing and preempting where possible. Use the dynamite wisely, for enemies you can't get into the purely-horizontal range of your gun.

211698.overview: A single screen at a time platfomer created by Anthony Vaugham Bartram  in 1994 and released to the public domain.

211708.overview: Repara Tronics is a clone of "Fix 'it Felix" developed by Amigatronics and released in 2019.

211719.overview: Something of a Pengo inspired game with really good title screen music. Roll-Out is a puzzle game that features a block pushing mechanic similar to Pengo. The game takes consists of one screen levels that are viewed from a top down perspective. On the screen there are various blocks that the player character (which is some sort of green little monster) can push (but not pull) and they will then move until they hit a solid object. Some of the blocks have smiley faces on them and the player's task is to push them onto hatch doors which will remove the blocks from the level. A level is completed once there are no more smilies on the screen. To make it all harder there are hostile creatures moving around that the player has to avoid touching since doing so will lead to a lost life. The enemies can be killed by pushing blocks over them but they will respawn after a while. There is also a time limit for each level.

211723.overview: Initially created using Backbone during AmiGameJam 2016, but with a couple of updates sincethen. Bruss Li's girlfriend has been kidnapped to keep him out of the martial arts tournament. So he puts on his yellow track suit unitard and goes to work on the baddies. He can be like water, flowing and unbreakable.

211791.overview: Realm of Sendai is an anime-influenced RPG for the Amiga computer. Adventure game a bit in style of Zelda (or Speris Legacy) with simple but working graphics. Contains Load / Save option.

211795.overview: A Polish 2D platformer heavily influenced by Doom and Obliterator. Created in 1994 by Sebastian Zieliñski of TSA. This game is a sequel to Rooster. Rooster II is a 2D side-scrolling shooter. The player's task is to annihilate an Eastern European terrorist group intending to use nuclear weapons. The mission starts at the roof of the enemy base. When redistributing grenades, ammo and Medi kits before each stage the player is limited by carrying the weight and number of available equipment. All those materials are scattered around the base and can be supplemented after defeating the numerous hosts of the enemy soldiers and robots. Controlled soldier can't run or jump, navigation consists only walking, quick walking, shooting, objects usage and items collection.

211834.overview: Rebel: G24 Solar System is a science-fiction real time strategy inspired by Dune II. The action takes place in the G24 star system, where the rebels took over the planet. As a lead commander the player must restore the order by expansion of the base, scientific research, gathering and proper use of military power and harvesting raw materials. The game features only one linear campaign with classic genre goals, such as harvesting an appropriate number of raw materials, repulsing the attack of the enemy troops or destroying the enemy base. The game allows multiple control of the troops. Building the facilities and the troops requires two types of raw materials: Materian occurring on trees and Belon located in the sand - both require another type of harvesting unit. Military units are divided into ground and air troops. More advanced facilities and units require laboratory research.

211841.overview:
Red Mars is a combination of real-time and turn-based strategy. Your main goal is to destroy the opposition (up to three players or CPU-controlled enemies can be played simultaneously) by achieving the highest level of technology possible. Gameplay is divided into two parts. In the RTS part you have to build new buildings, army, and prospect ground for minerals with a special unit called Pioneer. When you encounter enemy with your army, all combat becomes turn-based. The game has unique way of producing units. Each robot contains five parts: left hand, legs, torso, head and right hand. All can be combined to create almost an unlimited amount of different types of robots.

Multiplayer is available as play-by-email.

211875.overview:
Though the title is a pun on Rise of the Robots, this is a clone of Dynablaster. Up to four players may compete in a hunt for four stars hidden inside blocks, blowing up the blocks with their bombs — or blowing each other up. There are various other items on the screen, such as extra bombs, liquor bottles which reverse the controls, a gun to shoot blocks, speed-ups, a stop sign that halts all other players and a skul that makes you lose all you've picked up.

The game is only 32 kilobyte large, made for the 32k game competition at the Mekka & Symposium demo party in Fallingbostel, Germany.

211876.overview:
The first Rise of the Rabbits was a Dynablaster clone, but the second game is a simple platformer inspired by Super Mario Bros.

You guide your little rabbit, using the joystick button to jump (rather unorthodox for an Amiga game) across the side-scrolling landscape, jumping on baddies such as mushrooms and butterflies. You have a lot of inertia and can remain suspended for quite a long time compared to Mario, but jumps also require more precision since the main sprite is rather big compared to the background blocks.

The game has very little variation in the background blocks, since it is was made to fit in only 32 kilobytes, for the 32k games coding contest at the Mekka & Symposium demoparty, where the same team also released A-Type.

211880.overview: A military themed vertically scrolling shooter and sequel to Raid, created by Fez Software using the Shoot-'Em-Up-Construction Kit (SEUCK). It was described by the team as a SWIV tribute. This version is a little less difficult than the original, but the graphics are slightly improved. Tough, addictive and a bargain.

211884.overview: A 2D vertically scrolling military shooter created by Fez Software using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit.

211885.overview: The SEUCK based SWIV tribute game that is a sequel to Raid II: Mission X and the precursor to Raid IV: Super Raid. After your great victory in Mission X, you are again called upon to take out an EVD, a drug baron and his men, thus restoring peace to the people. Shoot anything that fires, collect civilians and peace through superior firepower!

211886.overview: The Sequel to Raid III: Total Fire and fourth and final game in the SEUCK based vertical shooter series. Raid 4 is perhaps the best the series had to offer. Another SWIV rip-off but very playable and deserving of attention. It suffers from hard difficulty level but is very worthy overall.

211890.overview:
Reverse is a board game, developed and published by Intersoft, which was released in Europe in 1993.

A Reversi or Othello variant played on a 16x16 grid. There is no music. You will play in contemplative silence against the computer, only interrupted by clicking sounds as more and more spaces on the board are claimed. Released via mail-order catalogue, on CD-ROM collections like Gamer's Delight 2.

211923.overview: The sequel to Armchair Assassin (The T.V. Chubbies in...). A highly entertaining murder simulator. Cute sprites burst from a wooden crate and run aimlessly in all directions. You move a crosshair and shoot at them with an arsenal of weapons and an endless amount of ammunition. Soon the screen is filled with blood, bones, and craters. You can change the music, the sounds, and even the sprites.

211957.overview: A competitive racing game with 3D polygon graphics. Not the most finished graphics, but a good multiplayer competitive experience with excellent controls.

211958.overview:
Although purporting to feature radio controlled cars, this is essentially a standard Super Sprint style racing game, which one or two players can join in. It's viewed from above, with the races lasting for 4 laps of close-quarters racing between 4 cars, with the computer providing the extras.There are 8 basic circuit layouts, featuring bridges, tight short-cuts, chicanes and hairpins.There are also arrow-shaped patches of ice which can cause the car to get away from you.The race ends when the leader finishes, with the other cars frozen on the spot and given their final positions based on where they are in that millisecond
 After you have completed the 8 tracks, you start on track 1 again. But this time it's gets harder.

211959.overview: A Chiplifter/Fort Apocalypse style 2D flying multi-directional shooter by Harald Müller and published in both Gamers' Delight and Gamers' Delight 2 compilations. Precursor to Rescue 2.

212027.overview: Rage is a shareware game for the Commodore Amiga. It can be best described as being similar to Universal Warrior, only without the shops. This is a top-down explorer and shooter, where you move around and shoot things to solve puzzles.

212028.overview: This Harald Müller shooter, which is similar to Gravitar is the sequel to Rescue, which was sort of a cross between Choplifter and Fort Apocalypse. Rescue II was published by both Intersoft and Schatztruhe in 1994.

212029.overview: Based on 1982 Carol Shaw/Activision Atari 2600 (commercial) release, RIVER RAID. A game viewed from a top-down perspective, flying a fighter jet over the River of No Return in a raid behind enemy lines.

212030.overview: Based on the 1984 C64 game 'Traffic', comes with a level editor. This version has support for up to three players simultaneously, three skill options, and 78 levels. A simple game where the player has to guide cars, motorbikes and buses through busy London streets by changing the traffic lights from red to green. The objective in order to advance to the next level is to get a preset number of vehicles through the screen, although it does not matter which exit you direct them through. Cars continue to queue off the edges of the screen (with numbers next to them if there are queued cars beyond your vision) and if the queue reach more than five cars, it's game over. A warning sound is given when five cars are queued; you must hope there are not also queues on surrounding roads. Cars always stay on their side of the road, and collisions are not possible.

212090.overview: A strategy game where the goal is to build a temple to the Pharaoh, it was developed by Christian Awizio of Cyberstyle and released on Amiga Fun 1992-03.

212091.overview: A war strategy game created by Zdenek Pletka and crew of the Cyber Alliance using AMOS and published in 1996.

212092.overview:
Alien Breed inspired 2-player split-screen deathmatch fun!

Choose from one of 6 battle-hardened mercenairies to do battle in one of 20 arenas in a fight to the death!

Old-school Amiga action in the Amiga .ADF file format for use with Emulators!

Featuring:
- Fake walls
- Jammed doors
- Power pickups

212093.overview: Robin Hood, but things have gone horribly wrong. Don't be surprised if you end up fighting dinosaurs. Robin Heed is an platform game, developed and published by Schatztruhe, which was released in Europe in 1993.

212094.overview: A Boulder-Dash style game written by Svante Berglund and Patrik Grip-Jansson of Terminus Team in 1993. One of the best Boulder Dash clones I have ever seen, but it's so damned brain-taxing that I only got this far. Scored 89% in The One and I can see why! in 2017 the original author re-released the full game as fully public domain with better two player support and 100 levels.

212148.overview: Released 1992-08-07 on Amigo! issue 1992-04. Running Bob is an platform action game, developed and published by Amigo!, which was released in Europe on  1992.

212149.overview: Roach Motel is a 1993 Amiga public domain platforming game, most notable to me as the very last game to work on my Amiga in the late 1990's, before it was put away for several years. There are around seventeen levels, any of which can be selected from the main menu.  You play as a funky looking character, with some mighty special teeth. Your main goal is to grab all of the spray paint cans scattered randomly throughout the levels, while avoiding or crushing the roaches which will spawn and disappear in an endless fashion. Similar to Ghosts and Goblins, these enemies have no issues spawning directly below you, causing some cheap deaths.

212187.overview: A puzzle game by Franz Janish of Stylong Crew with 30 levels of play.

212239.overview: A horror themed Beat'em Up game by B Bell, the sequel to the original Wrath of Gwendor and precursor to the Wrath Of Gwendor: Special Edition '97.

212284.overview: A Renegade style beat'em up created by Park Productions in 2000.

212291.overview: AMIGA The Rubber AGA Race game By Alberto Grecchi, a top down racing game.

212442.overview: Roper comes to earth in search of fuel for his ship. He lands his ship in the country. It's your goal to guide Roper from the country, to the city and then to a mine in search of fuel for his vessel to allow him to go home. It will be a tough journey. Avoid spiky traps, toxic waste and acidic explosions that will stand in your way.

212732.overview: Robo Ball is a game of American-style Football that is played with programmable robot players. It is a 2 player game and each player can individually set the plays for each of his offensive and defensive players. It follows many of the standard rules of football, but there are some differences. There are only six players on each side, the game lasts only 15 minutes, the robots cannot change their plays after they are set, etc.

212762.overview:
A Thrust / Gravitar style 2D shooter, R3: The Art of Rocketry is a video game written by Bruce Webster for the Amiga released in 1995. It was a playable demo on the coverdisks of Amiga Power (issue 54) in October 1995 and on Amiga Format (issue 89) in September 1996.

The game was initially released as shareware, but the author later released the full game as freeware on Aminet in 2000. The registered version included Tritus from Davin Pearson, a three-player competitive Tetris-inspired game, much in the same manner of the game Super Foul Egg. 

R3 is a Thrust clone where the player navigates a flying craft by rotating applying power in that direction. Vertical movement is affected by gravity.

R3 adds the ability to purchase new and better craft, which are organized into five classes. Each craft in the same class has similar characteristics, such as class 3 being large on the cargo space and shields, but low on missiles and low on thrust power. Each class has three craft within it, the weakest having lower everything (engine power, gun range, gun speed, cargo space, shields) but being much cheaper.

212778.overview: Team battle with tiny players, overhead view, ADF in the Zone. A team of small people fights against a team of small people on the field and at the desired speed. Now and then press the mouse button in the right place at the right time to gain a grab.

212779.overview: Puzzle game by William Bell of The Hidden released in 1992 and featured on Amiga Power 12, disk B.

212780.overview: Use BASIC language to program the movement of a remote robot, take and drop commands to have it pick up portable objects and to open locks along the way, read messages it finds and explore the world around it. Demo game created by Joona Palaste released in 1997. Later versions included support for playing your music in game and expanded BASIC support including POKE and PEEK.

212782.overview: Released as part of APC&TCP Volume 3 CD, this Homebrew game by Herbert was released in 1996. A multi-play party game with simple rules and easy to distinguish sides. See who can stay going the longest in this worm like variant.

212783.overview:
Ricochet v2.0 from Martin Longstaff on the Amiga was released in 1995.

The game is a table tennis/pong game with several difficulties and it's nicely presented.

212784.overview: A puzzle game featured on The One Amiga 50, disk B and the coverdisk of Amiga Computing 52, written by Colin Vella (Medina), Keith Bugeja (September).

212788.overview: A Spanish language homebrew shooter created by Miguel Ángel aka Jiménez Santana. A remake of the classic MSX 'Valkyr', this game proposes that you must try to annihilate any alien that crosses your path, in the purest 'Phoenix' style.  Programmed in AMOS it will give you a complex and addictive play. This game is based on a game called Valkyr that was released for MSX systems.

212790.overview: Return to Earth is an Adventure\role playing game, developed by Fantastic Simulations and published by Wolf, which was released in Europe in 1988. Released both commercially and as shareware. The game allows you to build up a very complex network of intergalactic trading routes as you attempt to track down the lost world of Earth.

212791.overview: A pong game, written in AMOS and set against a brutal science fiction background.

212792.overview:
Dark hours approaches mankind. Half of the population have succumbed to an epidemic of something very unpleasant, which like an uncontrollable nuclear reaction has spread itself across the planet Earth. Anarchy and Beat Kaalsson reigns among the survivors. Chaos prevails everywhere. The only spoken language is the naked, brutal and unmerciful language of violence. War sweeps over countries like tornadoes on rape-fields and devastates everything in its way. Is this the end of mankind? Is there really no hope? And does this have anything to do with the game?? The questions are just as many as they are stupid, and the answers are just as uncertain as what the future holds in its bosom.  
 
Game supports tournament play.

212793.overview: A technological remake of a 3500 year old design. A remake and update of Mancala, the transfer game, perhaps the oldest game known to man. Mancala is so widespread it is considered to be the most played game in most of Africa. Thousands of years ago, n many ancient lands, royalty and common men alike played games consisting of pits and using pebbles or jewels as playing pieces. Sometimes the games were played for high stakes, including rubies, sapphires and slaves. Ramify is based on these Mancala games. We believe you will find it as addictive as the kings and maharajahs of old found it and we have modernized it for your computer. In this version you are playing for megabytes of RAM chips.

212819.overview: A nice multi-direction scrolling shoot-em-up game similar to Asteroids or Photon Storm, created by Andreas Lunn and released in 1996.

212823.overview: A footrace game for up to 8 players, created by Ludde and Co and released in 1998. .

212824.overview: A public domain board game based on Monopoly for two to four players created by Jim Campey and Steve Howard in 1992.

212826.overview: 8-bit style game where you need to trap monsters into holes. It's remake of much older game. Your only chance of survival is to kill the aliens that reside on the planet. To achieve this you must first dig holes for the aliens to fall info. Once an alien has fallen into a hole, you must then fill in the hole that you have dug so that the alien falls to the ground below. Some aliens though, may need to fall through more than one level to die. Powerups are there to help, some help you wrap around screen, extra life, takes aliens up a platform, oxygen booster, extra points and swap a life in team game play, slow down aliens, speed boosts and more.

212827.overview: A homebrew, unauthorized sequel to the Amstrad\C64 Beat-em-up classic, made by first time game maker Nor Dean aka Nour.

212837.overview: Version 1.0 released, according to game installer notes on 9/9/1996 by Aaron McDonald, Solaris Software. Bounce the red ball around the arena and hit the stars while avoiding the blocks. Difficulty can be set by adding blocks.

212840.overview: Renegades is a two-player deatchmatch game seen from above. Two armed men must find and fight each other in a high-tech complex filled with bonuses, corridors and locked doors. Both graphically and layout-wise, it is very inspired by the Alien Breed series. On the technical side, it differs a lot from its graphical inspiration, with a horizontal split screen for each player.

213428.overview: A 2D puzzler game by Michael Taupitz, reminiscent of Lemmings and released as Shareware. Two versions of Right Way exists. The original version and a Easter Edition. It can be really, really difficult as there are no continues, no passwords, no saves and we have to restart from the first level if you die.

214264.overview: Rocket Attack is a vertical shooter, published by Softgang, which was released in Europe in 1987.

214412.overview: A shareware Othello board game created by Michael Koepke & Rolf Herrmann of BluesBrothers and released in 1992.

214504.overview: Walk around, dig holes, climb ladders and edit your own levels. This game is written in AMOS by Andreas Paschke and released in 1993.

214505.overview: Ragman, the game from Bonzai is a maze game where you have to collect the dots and reach the exit before the time runs out.

214506.overview: A freeware game from 1992 by Ben Ashley of Odyssey Software created in AMOS

214507.overview: The objective of the game is to make all the blocks in a level disappear. You do so by moving blocks with the same pattern together Game created by Emiel Lensink with level design from Ian (Exit 13).

214508.overview: A Pac-Man clone collect'em up with a bunch of new mazes to navigate, it was created by Videobrakkers Peace and released in 1991.

214509.overview: An update to the classic Pong game created as Shareware and released by Digital Design in 1993.

214510.overview: A 3+1 reel Fruit\Slot Machine game created by Stephen Eaborn with all the flashing lights goodness you would find on a real (or is that reel?) slot machine. With nudges and multiple betting lines and modes.

214511.overview: A homebrew slot\fruit machine game featuring 5 reel action, with 12 win lines from Tom & Kev.

214512.overview: A multi-directional scrolling shooter in the vein of Thrust or Gravitar created by Stephen Strickland and published in Amiga Format Issue #129 on the Cover CD in 1991. A level editor was included.

214513.overview: A commercially released version of the popular board game Reversi\Othello that was released in 1991 and created in AMOS.

214514.overview: Reversi is an implementation of the famous board game by Robert Brandner of Avalon and was released as part of the Pixel 128 GREEK MAGAZINE compilation.

214515.overview: A puzzle game by Aaron Fisher released by The Assassins and options to start on level 1, 25 or 50 to begin. In it you revolve the centers of the squares in blocks of four and attempt to match the centers with the outside to move on.

214519.overview: An isolated target practice subgame of the Eric Park Robocop game. Improve your skills and hit the target every time. I'd buy that for a dollar! Created by Eric Park of Park Productions and released in 1995.

214521.overview: A robotic platform shooter with 50 levels that was entered into the Amiga Format Blitz Basic Competition in 1994. Grab the goodies, shoot, jump or avoid the baddies. Clear the level of baddies to move on so grab that cake before you blast all the evil robots.

214522.overview: Take part as a robot in this platform game from Ben Marty, released as shareware in 1993. Full versions purchased could be had with an editor, if requested. Collect gems to buy items from an elf, collect keys to open doors of the same color, feathers slow your fall for a while. Rounded end blocks make floors until they encounter something. Elves sell keys of their hood color and other fun items. Spikes are deadly and there are secret blocks that must be bumped from below to reveal their treasures.

214523.overview: Program your robots better than your opponents and win the Arena! Released as part of the Assassins 04 games collection. It also came with a built in Program\Level editor.

214530.overview: A clone of Jet Set Willy created by S. Wattrs and T. Gilbert of ZSoft in 1995. As usual collect the goodies, avoid the baddies and spikes and make it to the next room.

214531.overview: Sets of 3 colored balls fall and you must match them, but there is a twist here to make things more interesting. A game written by Marc R. Miller and released as a homebrew game in 1994.

214533.overview: An AMOS base game from Tom Downes, released as an Amiga Format coverdisk in 1998, disk number 110. Simple and addictive spaceship game with 2 game types to play. Guide your ship safely to the next sector.

214534.overview: A Boulder dash clone created by Harald Müller (Mueller) for Schatztruhe and published in 1994. Pick up the jewels and avoid the falling boulders and use them to your advantage to take out the roaming nasties.

214536.overview: Another German language puzzle game created by Harald Müller (Mueller) and published by both Intersoft and Schatztruhe in 1994.

214537.overview: Game came with a level editor. Move the rocks to the marked places in a maze. You can only move one rock at a time. Things start off easily, but ramp up from there. Game created by Tobias Eckert in 1989.

214538.overview: A multi-scrolling shooter created by Mark Sheeky at Scorpius. Roton is a simple Asteroids-like game with the innovation of mouse control. Move the mouse right to rotate clockwise, and left for anticlockwise. Surreal enemies appear in increasing speed and quantity. I re-used this game dynamic many times. First in Xenex (1994), then Outliner (1996), and on PC with Roton (1999), Gunstorm (2005), and Gunstorm II (2006). The highly reactive control scheme was also used in my most popular PC game, Flatspace.

214539.overview: Designed and coded by The Assembly Line and scheduled for release in 1991. The finished game was going to include 40 levels of puzzle-solving fun against the computer, 2 player/demo modes, adjustable difficulty level, save game statistics for each level and level replays. A 3 level timed demo appeared on a dual format (ST/Amiga) coverdisk of The One (Issue 30, Mar 91). At the time the game did not have a publisher, thus the demo was designed to gauge how appealing a cerebral problem-solving game like this would be to potential buyers and publishers alike. Incidentally, neither the Amiga or Atari ST versions were thought to have ever released, but game disks have appeared now and again in the wild, and of course the magazine release did occur.

214540.overview: A roulette casino game created by Tokela, Donatello and Monotone of Calibra and released in 1992. Released at the Rebels and Complex Assembly 92 party. It was released as freeware.

214542.overview: A casino roulette game created by Ente Softproduction and released in 1990 by Schatztruhe in Schatztruhe #1227.

214543.overview: Another Harald Müller (Mueller) puzzle, another chance to listen to the title theme of Double Dragon 2! This one was released in 1994 and is a challenge to match the arrangement of blocks on the right with the blocks given in the rapidly decreasing time allowed.

214544.overview: Made available as a free download and developed by Kevin McGrory,  R-Squadron was originally created way back in the 90's as a top scrolling shooter that put you control of a small spaceship that had to avoid being wiped out from just about everything that appears on screen. The game is not for those who prefer the simple life, as many of the enemies such as turrets and "Exterminate" voiced creatures are deadly and can be hard to avoid.  “R-Squadron”, is created on the Amiga’s well known Shoot-Em-Up-Construction-Kit.

214545.overview: A freeware puzzle game created in 1993 and updated in 1994 by Ekke Verheul of ASWare. It was included in the Assassins 219 game pack along with Chopper Attack and Gimme 5. Travel through a world of roads. Use the arrow keys to walk around and try to get filthy rich fast. In most cases there is one UNDO possible and I know you're gonna use it!

214546.overview: A German language football management game featuring Ruhrpott area teams. The Ruhrpott is a large urban area in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is home to several large football clubs like FC Schalke 04, Borussia Dortmund or VfL Bochum. The two former clubs have been competing in international tournaments during the last couple of years. Borussia Dortmund was particularly successful, becoming either champions or runners-up in the Bundesliga German championship several times since 2010.

214547.overview: The sequel to Ruhrpott Fussball Manager from 2 years prior, this game was written in AMOS Pro and was released as a cover disk for the German Language, Amiga Future magazine. This is a German language, single player football management game released in 2000 written by Ander Wollny.

214548.overview: Released as part of the Five-Star PD Games Pack 22 and created by Simon Preene. The objective is the collection of sets of cards which share some property. The game is for either two or three players. A game consists of a number of hands where each player tries achieve a score lower than that of the other competitors. Default rounds are set to 7, but can be modified. 7 cards are dealt to each player and they take turns. Each players tries to get rid of all the cards in their hand by forming sets of 3 or more cards and submitting them or by adding cards to sets already submitted. Sets must consiste of 3 to 7 cards sharing a common attribute.

214549.overview: A Pac-Man clone by Rainer Wolf and released in 1990. New mazes to chomp your way through and frogs and animals to avoid instead of ghosts. Also no power pucks so this is much more about effective baddy avoidance.

214550.overview: A classical maze and puzzle game. You run around in a maze and try to catch the ghosts or spiders and to gather coins. Bombs can be used against baddies and to open up sections in the wall for further exploration. It is completely multitasking friendly and compatible with AmigaDOS 1.2/1.3 and 2.0. You can design your own levels. Binary only. Author: Jorrit Tyberghei. It was released as Shareware with a demo and a full version including source.

214552.overview: A freeware strategy shoot'em up game from Paul van der Valk, a luminary in Amiga game music. The most popular update, version 1.2 was released in 1996.

214895.overview: A combination of isometric adventure game and a dungeon crawler, with tons of unusual possibilities, contains various cities, spells, ship cruising, battling 2D and 3D (vector) enemies and much more. Quite hard and a manual is a must. All that is available online as the original commercial creators worked with the Amiga scene to make sure it was available to TOSEC and Hall of Light. Every game can be different as a random shuffling of the puzzle parameters happens at the start of each new game.

214945.overview: Reel Fish'n is a fishing simulator. Starting small in a rented boat with a plastic worm, a spinner, or other tackle, you can work your way to tournament status, purchasing not only additional tackle, but also equipment such as depth finders and serious bass boats. The player takes over a character's life, balancing business and fishing. Game elements include examining the weather forecast and deciding where to fish. Regular work needs to be done to provide money for the fishing hobby, or tournaments can be entered for financial support when they are won. Once a fish has been caught, it needs to be managed carefully to reel it in.

214946.overview: A Risk board game in English and German for four players for the Amiga, created by Frank Abbing of UAC Design and published in shareware form with a Demo version and a full version.

214951.overview: When started you'll see a playfield on the left. On top of the playfield you'll see the text Press F Keys for Money. F1 is $10, F2 is $20, F3 is $50, F4 is $100, F5 is $250, F6 is $1000 and F7 is $5000. Use the mouse to indicate where to bet and press the left button, a coin will appear to mark your bet. A total of 40 bets may be made. F10 starts a new round. Press U to undo, S to toggle sound. There is a built in Help screen.

215015.overview: This action puzzle game from George Broussard was akin to a more intellectual Boulderdash where you must travel many trapped and tricky caverns to find the three ancient Rings of Zon to help defeat Korak, the Dark Lord and practitioner of the black arts. While you are just a sorcerer's apprentice, you are chosen by the Council of Magicians to take up this difficult task.

215016.overview: Unofficial fan-made sequel to ROBOCOP 3, written using AMOS. Tonight's headlines on Mediabreak... Reports that after ten years as a museum piece, the first cyborg law enforcement unit "ROBOCOP" mysteriously came back on-line and broke free from it's preserving case. It is now roaming the corridors of the Delta City museum. In related news, Omni Consumer Products current line of robot cops are today still executing offenders for minor offenses. An OCP spokesman had this to say - "We are aware of the glitch and hope to have all Law Enforcement Droids programming thoroughly checked in a few weeks time.

215041.overview: Rooster is a 2D top-down shooter with puzzle elements which visually resembles the game Alien Breed. The player's task is to annihilate terrorists from Mars who have taken over a science base on the moon, where the best Earth scientists conducted research on new types of weapons. Terrorists have taken over the space station's defense robots which treat our commando as a hostile. In addition to the enemies, you come across various interactive elements, such as mobile missiles, mines, generators, turbines, scientists. The game consists of four extensive levels.

215095.overview: Ran Trainer is a German language sports management game, developed and published by Greenwood, which was released in Europe in 1995.

215137.overview: Roulette-Royal is a roulette casino game, developed by Magic Soft, which was released in Europe in 1990.

215229.overview:
A platform game by Gianluca Sclano. The aim of the game is to be able to save your father (Radanelli Senior) from the clutches of a mysterious kidnapper (Mr X).
In this adventure you will have to face an army of Mr. X's henchmen, who have undergone genetic mutations when subjected to dangerous radiation.
You will have to search far and wide in all the places where your father has enemies, and defeat the forces of evil present ...

215232.overview: A promotional game sponsored by Play Video, the football\soccer game is based on the footballer Fabrizio Ravanelli and was released in 1994.

215236.overview: Eliminate all the setup and takedown time, save yourself hours of tedium and trade for hours of fun for you and up to 4 friends playing the conversion of the classic board game Risk! on your Amiga computer.

215322.overview:
A top-down vertically scrolling 2D shooter created by Martin Ludwig and Sebastian Ulrich of Cachet and published by Rainbow Arts in Europe in 1988.

Also known as Revenge of Doom.

215383.overview: Jump over the gravestones, avoid the wandering monster. Once you jump over all the gravesites you move to the next level!

216779.overview:
Realm of the Warlock is a text adventure with graphics for the Amiga.

Ashton is now a desolate place ruled by the strongest. Before the region was seized, several wise elders controlled the land. As Ashton matured, word of its prosperity spread throughout the world, and many came to ponder this glorious land. Then, as the elders gathered in the town of Fairshire, they were were abducted by a user of black arts. Without the wisdom of the Elders, Ashton quickly became troubled. You alone decided to search the hall in which the Elders were last seen, and came across the mysterious scroll responsible for the Elder's abduction. You have been brought into the Realm of the Warlock, and must save the kidnapped Elders.

Text adventure with graphics. All commands are via VERB NOUN entry. There is a save and restore option.

216970.overview:
Rommel at El Alamein is a computer wargame for multiple systems, covering World War II battles in Egypt from 30 June to 8 November 1942.

Players can control the Allied and/or German sides, or the computer can take on one or both roles. The game is text-only, and originally came with a board and physical pieces to allow the player to keep track of the location of theirs and enemy units. Each turn, the player has access to the intelligence menu, where they can see a list of currently held territory, gains, and losses. This menu also includes weather forecast, player and enemy strength, available supply, and recent losses. The player can allocate supplies and set movement orders for individual units including: hold, move, and attack.

Game time is divided into morning, afternoon, and evening each day of play. Games can be saved in progress, and loaded at a later date.

217269.overview: The game demo is called Red 41 The Silent Death and has the protagonist of a robot very reminiscent of Appleseed (you know the cop with the antennas?); this game remembers, at least in the graphic style of the backgrounds and choice of colors. Occasionally you will even fly with the your robot. Some say the game is closer to Genocide 2 from the X68000. The Demo was released in The Games Machine Settembre Numero 56 in 1993.

217301.overview:
In the year 2090, Earth is invaded by extra-terrestrials. The World Alliance of Nations has developed a supersonic attack fighter, Raiden, to defend the Earth. A pilot must take control of the experimental fighter to destroy the alien warships that just happen to look like odd variations of typical military tanks and planes with gadgets attached to them.

Raiden is an over-head vertical-scrolling shooter, based on an arcade game of the same title. It features two forms of weapon upgrades and two types of missiles (normal or homing). You start the game with several bombs which you can use to destroy most enemies on the screen to get yourself out of a jam. Each level ends with a large boss or bosses.

Game finished and reviewed but not released by U.S. Gold as they went under before it could be distributed. Recovered from the original DAT tapes beginning in 2004 by one of the coders.

223486.overview: The game was originally developed by Core Design (Simon Phipps) and published by Firebird in 1989 and this version which is a backport of the Nintendo Wii edition (remake  by Magic Team) with  32 color palette which is getting a graphical overhaul in development for the Amigamejam competition.

223566.overview: Ring around the World is a short, open world, bird's-eye view, point'n'click adventure where the protagonist wakes up on the shores of an unknown world with just two memories - one being of himself drowning in a stormy sea.

417666.overview: A German language joystick waggler with a track and field theme. Apparently, it was developed by a teacher at a centre for computer courses. Players select from a roster of three rats, then they are off to the stadium. The race lasts for a couple of seconds. Depending on the score, players may be able to enter their initials on the high score table. Afterwards, the game returns to the title screen.

418036.overview:
A mech strategy wargame for one to 6 users released to public domain in 1990. Robot simulates a fight between heavy robots up to 18 meters high. Each player can choose 1-6 robots with different characteristics. You can choose:
FISTHAWK can kick and punch in all directions and negates mines. 
YETI feels most comfortable in the mountains, 
THUNDERWEEL shouldn't get too close to the water. 
ANTIMEYER is immune to MOVEKILLER and BIG TOASTER. 
HOBBIT is immune to mine explosions unless he's into it.
Menu controls: Player1 cursor left, cursor right, spacebar Player2 joystick left, right, fire button press mouse button.

418434.overview:
An Open Source Conversion by Iantus360 of this Doom style 3D FPS game. A madman with power to kill millions has been discovered, and HUNT (High-risk United Nations Taskforce) has been dispatched to discover his plans. Your team was infiltrating his island stronghold when everything went to hell. The infiltration boat exploded and fire came from all directions. The only way out is in, into the the fortress, but to stay out here would be certain death. So in you go, guns blazing...

Rise of the Triad, a first-person shooter, is the successor of Wolfenstein 3D, with a somewhat improved 3D engine. Everything is still composed from blocks, but multiple vertical levels have been added; there are stairs made of platforms floating in air, and jump pads which launch you (and the enemies) high up so that you can walk over tall barriers in your way.

The game offers a lot of weapons. You begin with a pistol, but later you can find an extra pistol for John Woo-style shooting, and a MP40 rifle. All these weapons have unlimited ammo. You can also find more potent weapons - from classic rocket launcher, to quite wacky contraptions such as a "drunk missile" launcher or the "Excalibat", a powerful baseball bat. However, you can carry only one such a strong weapon at a time, and they have limited ammo.

Enemies are mostly humans equipped with various weapons. Their attacks can be quite varied; some of them can steal your weapons (though you can retrieve them after killing them), other shoot nets at you that trap you (you have to wriggle out, unless you found a knife, which will allow you to cut your way out). Apart from enemies, you'll be endangered by fireball launchers, rolling boulders and crushing walls.

There's a lot of power-ups you can pick up. They all have various wacky effects: for example, "God Mode" makes you immortal and allows you to toss homing, insta-death missiles; "Dog Mode" turns you into a... dog, which can fit into small spaces (and is inexplicably invulnerable to weapons); "Shrooms Mode" makes everything shine with bright colours, as if you were on drugs; "Elasto Mode" makes you very prone to bouncing off walls when you run into them.

418435.overview: A 3D adventure game by C. Millin, where you pilot a mini-sub to the wreck of the Titanic. Made in 3D Construction Kit, however this game is very responsive even on un-expanded A1200.

418439.overview: An open source conversion by BSzili and created by Franticware for the #hvdosdev2021 competition at https://www.high-voltage.cz where it won the first place, this is a 3D rally racing simulator.  You control a small RC car on various terrains and race against time. Frca kindly agreed to share the source code, so it became a nice weekend project to get it running on the Amiga. The original game DOS needs an 486 DX with 8 MB RAM, and the Amiga version has similar requirements. To play it you'll need a 68040 or 68060 with an FPU, 8 MB Fast RAM, AGA chipset or RTG. When you pass between checkpoints marked with green blocks, the display shows if you are behind or ahead of the track record. I like how the car's suspension visibly reacts to bumps in the track. The game saves your lap times, and gives trophies for beating the top times Normal and Reverse; which is really addictive. The RC car feels light, and can roll over on the 6 different landscapes in the game; where you can press ESC if you want to abort a run.

418457.overview: A horizontally scrolling shooter created by New Deal Productions, like a fast paced version of Microcosm. Converted from the Atari ST version by the original developers.

418461.overview: A Finnish maze game with obstacles created in AMOS by the Solaris group and released in 1992. Find your way through incredible tracks and collect a treasure of energy. Special obstacles make it difficult for you to travel.

418551.overview: Computer game version of Rubik's Clock puzzle, created by Sphinx and published by CompuTec Verlag in 1989. The object of the game is to set all the clocks at 12:00 by pushing and turning the buttons.

418660.overview: A text adventure with still pictures with an educational theme. The game features a number of islands connected by bridges, and each bridge has a troll living on it that will only let you pass if you answer a logic problem correctly.

419544.overview: A maze game with RPG elements from Micro Fix released in 1990. Important note for playing on emulators: Turn your joystick emulation off, in order not to block the Amiga numpad! Game can solely be controlled with numeric keypad, utilizing all keys from 1-9. To liberate Land Zon from the claws of the sinister Korak and his demon spawn, you fend off enemies charging from all sides while you find keys, refresh your life energy or collect symbols for sword strikes or teleporter jumps. Although these symbols increase your own combat power enormously, they can only be used to a limited extent. Despite everything, you will not reach the next level by killing enemies alone, a little strategic evasion and skillful handling of supplies is also essential.

420142.overview: ​Released in arcades in 1987, Taito’s Rastan was one of the best fantasy action-platformers of its time. Now, after eight months down in the basement, the Amiga version of Rastan emerges. This is a demo of the first level, featuring remastered sprites and brand new, reimagined backgrounds, all running on a stock Amiga 500 with 512kb extra ram!

420276.overview:
RANA - Reckless Amphibian New Adventures
A Frogger clone for Commodore Amiga OCS/ECS

420704.overview:
challenging, procedurally generated, roguelite twin-stick shooter for the Classic Amiga platform!
The wizards have been at it again, and this time they've accidentally opened Hellgates under the castle! Now it's up to you, brave, brave Sir Declan, to search each procedurally generated castle dungeon and find enough magical shards to access and close its gate.
Armed with a magical Caster Sword, potions you find, and perhaps the occasional legendary charm, Sir Declan must fight demons that escaped from the gate, avoid traps, and collect treasures to trade for battle enhancements, before finally facing the Hellgates themselves.

420708.overview:
SCENARIO:

The dungeons of Moredecoom await...

For time immemorial, legend has told of a dark, deadly dungeon containing unimaginable horrors and riches beyond belief. Enough riches and magic to make you a king... or more...

You have searched for this dungeon ever since you stumbled upon the legend in an Egyptian library many years ago. It started with the rumor of an ancient dark being and a magic amulet. The legend tells of an awakening and of unspeakable horrors to come. Your search carried you across the world, one riddle at a time.

Through many trials and perils, you are now standing at the entrance of a dark and mystical dungeon far from where you started. You, Zendar, a fighter, a mage, or uh, a rogue, are ready to defeat the monsters and gather the riches waiting below.

You just need to take a leak first...



FEATURES:

-  Fully procedurally-generated levels
-  A unique experience with every playthrough
-  A plethora of potent potions and pickups
-  Glorious pixelated isometric graphics
-  Atmospheric soundtrack by Jogeir Liljedahl
-  Gruesome sound effects by h0ffman
-  No easter eggs - just lots of chickens.

420874.overview:
Little top down car racing game for Classic Amiga computers inspired by Rally Cross DOS game. Source code can be downloaded free. 

Rally Coss is a collective effort from the following people:
Ozzyboshi: concept and code
Vectrex28: fonts Z3K / Tracks and background images
Lunix: Tracks and menu music
Oriens: Tracks Maze / mod.alfetta background music
O. Stokka (4pLaY): Coordination

420887.overview: A demo of the Kingsoft game that was to be released, there are indications that this was to be the sequel to Mike The Magic Dragon and was coded by Frank Neuhaus. The background tune used in the options screen is based on a sample from Jan Hammer's 1985 award-winning Miami Vice soundtrack, "Crockett's Theme".

420911.overview: RAGS is intended to feel like a deluxe version of the last level of the C64 game Beach Head 2. The plot is simple: Two guys face each other in an arena trying to kill each other. This goal can be achieved by knifes, portable rocket launchers, mini-guns or by luring the opponent into a trap. The game can be played against a computer opponent, which was designed long before we had our first lecture in Artificial Intelligence, and is therefore not too smart, but the real fun starts when You play against a friend.

420915.overview: Rooper: The World Of Logic is a playable demo, the final game was never released but the demo for this platforming game was out in 1998 from Gleaming Design.

420920.overview:
"Razor" is an horizontally scrolling shoot-em-up at the moment, but
I will include stages of vertically scrolling too. It's very classic stuff,
with power-ups, end-of-level guardians and interesting graphics. I'm trying
to put a nostalgic feeling to it, making a resemblance to good old Amiga
games of 1990-91, like R-Type, Z-Out, and the superb Project-X.The last is
hard to beat, but I wanna make my game the best as I can.

420945.overview: Ragnov was the first game project of Softeyes in the late 1980s. A 2D sideways multi-directionally scrolling shooter. They did create a demo and sent that to several publishers, but the game never worked out and they started working on Hoi . Ragnov featured parallax scrolling and a split-screen mode for two players. The game's concept was processed into Hoi level 3 (where Hoi flies around with a jetpack on his back).
