420979.overview: This Game is called Realm of Maiyessae from 1989, by Jennifer Diane Reitz in S.E.U.C.K.

421222.overview: Sample game written with Backbone and AMOS released as part of the Backbone shareware package in 1999. Backbone is a powerful multitasking tool to create games without programming skills. Backbone allows you to design a variety of games; Scrolling or non-scrolling platform games, vertical and horizontal shooters and games viewed from above.Backbone allows you to design a variety of games; Scrolling or non-scrolling platform games, vertical and horizontal shooters and games viewed from above. Backbone includes 4 example games including Reality as one of them, sounds, graphics and documentation in AmigaGuide format.

421272.overview: A playable demo game developed by Hexmage960. It is a clone of the Atari 8-bit classic Robbo.

421287.overview: Unreleased remake of the classic H.E.R.O., based on the c64 port.

421381.overview:
Drive the Space Rover around the maps, find the reactors and destroy them 
to allow the captive to escape. The Captive must reach the teleport,
followed by you, before the timer expires to proceed to the next level.

422239.overview:
Race with your red car trying to beat the clock while you avoid the other cars and many obstacles on the road. Collect wrenches and money bags for extra score and drive very fast to beat all 20 stages!  EASY is slower and time limits are less tight. The game was designed with "HARD" being the "normal" difficulty. 

Wrenches are worth 10000 points but they raise value for each one collected, up to 20k points. Miss one and it resets to 10k. Money bags are worth 25k. When you get a checkpoint you get bonus points for the time left, later levels give more points for each second left. Game save high scores on floppy (leave it write-enabled!) and high scores for HARD and EASY level are kept separated.

422259.overview: A single player shooter created with SEUCK and published as freeware by Courbois Software in 1991. Finish off that pizza and take your sai weapons as we are going into the tunnels to take on ninjas, mole men and other baddies. Clear them out and make Master Splinter proud!

422261.overview:
Radar Rat Run is an unofficial 16-bit clone of the Commodore VIC-20 and C64 game Radar Rat Race, which in turn were also clones, of Namco's Rally-X. This version was written in AMOS, was developed by Stephen Williams and released into the public domain in 1995. You control a ratty, who must grab all the pieces of cheese in a maze, and flee from all the other rats. Once you reach a barrier in the maze, you are automatically rotated, but you can always manually change direction. There are red ones who chase after you, and black ones who are activated when you get close to them - both types kill you on contact. When they are close, you can activate a Star Screen to block them off.

The Radar of the title is on the right of the screen, and shows you where each piece of cheese is, although the actual maze is not illuminated, so your next snack might be further away than you think.

422264.overview: Relayer is a two player competitive Qix clone for the Amiga. It was developed by Antonio Argentieri and released into the public domain in 1993.

422265.overview: Ring War is a pseudo vector based shooter similar to the arcade classic, Star Castle. It was developed by Eric Bazan and released as Charityware in 1991. Shoot the target in the middle by disabling its protective shield.

422269.overview: A single player puzzle game from Mark Archer, created with AMOS and published in Amiga User International. Released as part of the Amiga Classix 5 compilation. This is a color matching puzzle game.

422270.overview: Rough Waters is a vertically scrolling shooter for the Commodore Amiga, it was developed by VSC Productions using the Amiga version of the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit, and released into the public domain in 1994.

422272.overview: A  freeware Tron\Snake like game from Chris Gregan of Hung Like a Hamster in 1998.

422365.overview: A run and jump game from Johnny Acevedo from 2012. Published in the freeware Amiten Software CD Volume 1 - by Amiten (surprisingly). Contains three games - Fish, Spacer Remake and Run Puff as well as demos of AmiKill and AmiVania.

422421.overview: This program by Terry Fike is a colorful mix of adventure and role-playing games with a good dash of humor. It's about finding treasure on an island threatened by the flood. You are confronted with various problems that make life difficult (rising water levels, hunger, traps, etc.). It was released as freeware in 1989.

422694.overview: A single player platform game by Digital Soft Productions released as public domain in 1988.

422755.overview: An action game made by Anbjorn Myren using the Hollywood game system with version 1.25 released in 2021.

422995.overview: RESHOOT PROXIMA III has been developed by Richard Löwenstein, Kevin Saunders, and Altraz Virgill with many features we expect from some of the team behind the excellent Reshoot R series. Features such as lots of blasting action, a cool soundtrack, deadly enemies, 5 uniquely themed stages, 24 bit color pixel art, a steady 50 fps frame rate, and much much more you'll just have to experience for yourselves if you have a Commodore Amiga A1200, A4000 and CD32.

423201.overview:
Fame and Wrath:
Germany in 1648,  30 years of war had devastated the country, destroyed the cities, displaced the people, destroyed the wealth. The Peace of Westphalia ended this power struggle. The reconstruction of the country can begin. You are 20 years young and are starting your journey from being an apprentice assistant in a trade. The house of the Hanseatic in the city of Lübeck  is now the largest shipowner in the world, who can afford to humiliate emperors and kings. Money gives you power over the most powerful in the world. It all started with a small inheritance of your deceased father.  You are now at the beginning of an adventurous climb! Begin your journey to become the most powerful merchant in the land

423228.overview: A freeware AMOS game from Amiten (Johnny Acedvedo and Phornee de goblins doing music) for the Amiga 500. Fire torpedoes at underwater threats and missiles at surface threats and be king of the seas.

423338.overview: An AMOS based, freeware fighting game based on the Rocky IV movie where you must fight Drago, a six-foot-four, 261-pound fighter who has the backing of the Soviet Union. the game was made by Daniel Clinton and published in 1996.

423353.overview: A freeware Wheel of Fortune game puzzle for one or two players created by Beaty Softworks in 1993. Spin the wheel, get scored the amount on the wheel times the number of letters you guess. Buy a vowel if needed, but lose points. Avoid bankruptcy if you can!

423384.overview: What if?! What if Barbarian had been an endless runner instead of a beat-'em-up. Then you would have this game by Johnny Acevedo of Amiten Software in 2019.

423411.overview: This single player demo puzzle game has 2 modes of difficulty, where you must avoid the Amiga ball and add your memory to the memory expansion board as in real life, the more RAM you have, the better! Game by CIS and released as freeware in 1989.

423499.overview: Do you have what it takes to be a champ? Find out in this single person boxing game released as freeware in 1992. In the game you work your way to the championship by fighting lower ranked fighters in the style of Punch Out. Your first fight is against John Vein Sucker and make your way to the a title bout.

423511.overview:
Raptor Call Of The Shadows Amiga Version

After completing each level you have the option of upgrading your ship with a powerful arsenal of weapons and goodies. Some weapons are effective on only ground or air targets, while some are on both. There are some really advanced weapons like the auto-track mini-gun which can effectively destroy almost any kind of targets without aiming the ship.

Dying in shoot'em ups can be annoying, especially if you have to start all over the beginning. However, in Raptor you can save your game between each level. If you have enough credit you can even buy multiple shields for further protection.

423537.overview:
The key was inserted into the ornate lock and as it settled into place there was a gentle "click" ... Smith gripped the key and slowly turned it to the left but nothing happened. Taking a deep breath, he turned the key to the right and for a moment felt resistance to his pressure, then suddenly the lock clicked into place. Placing a hand on either end of the lid Smith carefully lifted it open.

Twenty seven years he had waited for this moment, twenty seven years of searching and wishing, twenty seven years of danger, hardship and deprivation. But now it could all be over ...

Leaning forward, Smith peered into the small casket and an immense wave of relief swept over him as he spied the small yellow spheroid nestling at the bottom of the casket.

SEVEN DAYS EARLIER ...

423553.overview:
Even more difficult trivia question about the British science fiction comedy franchise created by Rob Grant and Doug Naylor, which primarily consists of a television sitcom that aired on BBC Two between 1988 and 1999. This championship version was released as freeware, in 1997. 

The main setting of the series is the eponymous mining spaceship Red Dwarf. In the first episode, set sometime in the late 21st century,[a] an on-board radiation leak kills everyone except lowest-ranking technician Dave Lister, who is in suspended animation at the time, as punishment for smuggling a cat aboard the ship. The cat, Frankenstein, who is revealed to be pregnant, is safe in the cargo hold. Following the accident, the ship's computer Holly keeps Lister in stasis until the radiation levels return to normal—a process that takes three million years. Lister therefore emerges as the last human being in the universe—but not alone on board the ship. His former bunkmate and immediate superior Arnold Judas Rimmer (a character plagued by failure) is resurrected by Holly as a hologram to keep Lister sane. They are joined by a creature known only as Cat, who was initially thought to be the last member of a race of humanoid felines that evolved in the ship's hold from Lister's pregnant cat during the three million years that Lister was in stasis

423570.overview:
A trivia quiz game written in Blitz Basic by David Anderson and published by Astro Software in 1995. The quiz is centered on a UK sci-fi show and all the nuggets of information about it. The cat, Frankenstein, who is revealed to be pregnant, is safe in the cargo hold. 423591.overview:
A top-down, turn based strategy game for 1 to 6 players, by Ralf Peters, published by Markt & Technik in 1989. Regnum means Kingdom. 
Regnum is your kingdom in an imaginary world consisting of countries, lakes, mountains and cities. The Amiga mouse serves as your scepter. Your task: Secure and expand your property with the help of political, economic and military actions. But reality quickly catches up with you: in this game, too, the economy and the military are depressingly closely interwoven with each other. 449921.overview:
It's you against the clock in Rotar, a game of strategy that requires a keen mind and a joystick. Fifty levels are ready to challenge you. Each is a unique puzzle.

Rotar places you in a grid of disks. One disk has a red plus sign on it. This is the hot disk. (In higher levels, there may be more than one hot disk.) Your goal is to rotate the disks so that the tubes on the disks are all connected to the hot disk. Of course there's a trick that keeps the game from being trivial — you can only travel between disks if there's a direct connection between the two.

To play, double-click on the Rotar icon, which can be found in the Rotar directory of the Resource disk. Rotar will load the file, Rotar.dat, containing the 50 levels. When the levels have loaded, you'll be playing the first level.

457406.overview:
At age 16, I spent about 6 months coding a Wheel of Fortune clone in AMOS on my Commodore Amiga. I then updated it from college at Virginia Tech, using my Amiga 3000UX that was a requirement as a CS student at the time.

Provided is the original LHA file for Rueda 1.3e, which crazily enough, is still available on Aminet after I uploaded it 31 years ago! You just need to expand the LHA, assign RUEDA: to the DATA folder, and then run the Rueda! executable. I am guessing I could have made that process more elegant. It seems kinda bananas to me now to expect someone to do that extra step in a terminal to play the game.

It blows my mind that I didn't finish another game until 30 years later, because I *love* making games. Much like comics, they utilize a wide array of creative arts that I enjoy: sound design, music, drawing, UI, logic, typography, movement, animation, etc. They're also similar to comics in that you can spend years on something that someone might give 5 minutes of attention to, if you're lucky!

Strangely I think this game holds up (despite the painful "CATAGORY" typo, good lord). It seems unlikely to me now that I made the title music, but who knows, I stumbled through making a li'l theme song for Save Picoville in Pico 8. The very hip hop '90s sound effects crack me up. Also the puzzles are pretty weak. But hey, I was 16.

Here I am with my A500 and external hard drive without a cover, and a fan cooling it along with the 1200 baud modem in the back (I ran a BBS called The Real Flavor at the time):

I was gifted an Armiga years ago, which is basically a 3.5" floppy disk with a Cubieboard attached running Android, and it can digitize old Amiga floppies. I've been toting around a wooden box full of floppies for decades, and though many barfed, I was able to extract several ADFs from my ancient collection. I found several mockups indicating the start of Rueda 1.4 (see below), which I apparently abandoned as soon as I sold my Amiga 1200. I must have had the A1200 for only a few months, as I don't remember it at all.

I do love my lightswitch UI graphics, and was pleased to see that I realized my error in not just using plain colors on the spinning wheel. I think I painstakingly drew out all the numbers on a large version of the wheel in DeluxePaint, so was hellbent on using that work, even if it completely fell apart when shrunk down in v1.3. Anyway, v1.4 was going to fix that error, as well as support 4 players with custom avatars, but I don't think I ever got further than these mockups.

461919.overview:
You are piloting a hovercraft equipped with a special magnetic generator, and your goal is to push a metal sphere—rolling across the playing field—into your opponent's goal by utilizing the magnetic force emitted by your craft. The craft is equipped with eight thrusters, each activated by moving the joystick in the desired direction. Thanks to the air cushion, friction is virtually non-existent; consequently, any thrust generated either increases or decreases the craft's speed, whereas the speed remains constant when no thrusters are engaged. To come to a stop, you must fire the thrusters opposite to your direction of movement. The craft changes direction upon contact with the field boundaries or the opponent's craft. The ball cannot be physically struck, as it rolls along the floor while the craft hovers on an air cushion just above the surface. To deflect the ball, you manipulate the craft's magnetic field: the magnetic force repels the ball or attracts it (depending on the polarity setting), thereby altering its trajectory. The force acting on the ball is governed by the laws of physics.
